name: Substrate world-knowledge fact recall via LEX semantic-constant retrieval
description: Substrate-only world-knowledge fact recall via LEX semantic-constant retrieval. Mechanism: substrate POS/NER (existing Tier-A) extracts entity-attribute from query; cleanup retrieval against pre-stored substrate LEX subset (unit conversions, calendar facts, geographic facts, time facts) recovers factual constants. DISTINCT from PP-394 ASDiv math-WK content domain (substrate-product diversity within LEX_T mechanism). Empirically validated Cycle 52 HARD_PASS isolation: 100 facts + 10 trials + D=4096. LEX_T acc 0.979 / held-out 0.970 vs discriminative-perceptron baseline 0.600 acc / 0.010 held-out. NOISE-ROBUST: +0.379 lift at noise 0.0 -> +0.574 at noise 2.4 (perceptron degrades; LEX_T cleanup retrieves clean prototypes). Held-out facts perceptron at CHANCE (0.010 among 50 answers) = structural impossibility absent pattern; LEX_T retrieves from stored knowledge. Substrate-product positioning MAJOR: semantic memory vs pattern-learning -- substrate retrieves stored constants while LLMs hallucinate untrained facts. Critical substrate-self-improvement role: 2nd LEX_T capability triggers discriminative_perceptron -> lex_semantic_constant_retrieval recurring rule (with PP-394 post-unification) = Tier 5 FOURTH-APPEARANCE. Brain analogue: Tulving 1972 semantic memory + Patterson-Nestor-Rogers 2007 ATL semantic hub + ventral stream object-knowledge.
